title: Private upgrade rollback loop caused by external secret TLS rotation and operator circuit-breaker
creator: Ava Martinez
description: During a customer private/VPC upgrade to runtime-1.18, multiple clusters entered a Helm rollback loop. Upgrades repeatedly failed during post-deploy validation: nodeagents and webhooks flapped and controllers hit operator-level circuit-breakers, preventing reconciliation and leaving workloads in a degraded state. Customer reported service disruption for model inference and inability to apply configuration changes.
repro_steps: 1) Start on-prem upgrade from chart v1.2.8 to v1.3.0 in a cluster with ExternalSecretOperator installed
2) Helm applies new values; new TLS secrets are expected to be present in namespace redwood-system
3) ExternalSecretOperator rotates TLS secret asynchronously; timing mismatch causes controller pods to restart while helm postinstall job performs validation
4) Operator detects transient webhook failure and trips a circuit-breaker that marks CRs as 'reconcile-failed', triggering Helm rollback
5) Rollback removes new resources but ExternalSecretOperator continues rotation, keeping TLS in flux -> loop
investigation_summary: - Initial signals: repeated helm release history showing upgrade -> failed -> rollback -> upgrade attempts.
- Logs: webhook server logs show TLS handshake errors coincident with secret update timestamps.
- Operator behavior: built-in circuit-breaker threshold (5 consecutive webhook failures within 30s) was too aggressive for environments where ExternalSecretOperator updates secrets during upgrades.
- Config drift: some clusters had manual secret annotations (external-managed: true) that prevented deterministic ordering in Helm hooks.
- Correlation: customer clusters using ExternalSecretOperator and pod-level admission webhooks were the only ones affected.

- Root cause: race between Helm upgrade hooks and external secret rotation combined with a conservative operator circuit-breaker and Helm pre/post hooks that validated webhook availability synchronously.
mitigation: - Short-term: advised customers to temporarily pause ExternalSecretOperator autosync for the redwood-system namespace before starting upgrades.
- Emergency hotfix: ship operator change that treats transient TLS handshake errors as retriable and extends circuit-breaker window (PR #1289).
- Rollforward plan: add a Helm pre-upgrade hook that checks for secret stability for 30s before applying chart changes.
- Support playbook: added a runbook step to detect TLS rotation events during upgrades and to trigger a controlled retry instead of rollback.
- Customer communication: notified active escalations with instructions and offered a coordinated upgrade window with Redwood SRE
fixes: - github.com/redwood-inference/operator PR #1289: make webhook TLS failures retriable, bump circuit-breaker thresholds
- github.com/redwood-inference/charts PR #342: pre-upgrade check for external secret annotations and optional pause signal
- released hotfix build private-2026.03.13-hotfix (operator image: redwood/operator:1.3.1-hotfix)

postmortem_next_steps: 1) Permanent fix: redesign operator webhook backoff to detect secret-rotation semantics instead of static circuit-breaker thresholds (owner: Platform Runtime).
2) Add pre-upgrade gating in Helm charts to coordinate with ExternalSecretOperator via an annotation-based pause handshake (owner: Charts Team).
3) Documentation: document ExternalSecretOperator compatibility notes in Private deployment upgrade docs and add checklist for customers (owner: Docs).
4) Runbook: bake the temporary pause pattern into the upgrade runbook and update automation to set annotation automatically when customer requests a scheduled upgrade (owner: SRE).
5) Retro: customer-specific postmortem shared with affected accounts and account teams; capture contractual SLA mitigation if needed.
